title: TrustOperationEvidenceBundleV1
description: The supplied evidence a plan (plan.schema.json) is checked against to produce a report (report.schema.json). Frozen per issue #1714, checkpoint 1 revision 2. v1 authenticates no external collector: it checks internal consistency against declared provenance only, and says so. The definitions.context_identity block here MUST stay byte-identical to the same-named definition in plan.schema.json (tests/trust_operation_v1_contract.rs asserts this).

operation_id.description: Must match the bound plan's operation_id; a mismatch is invalid_evidence, checked by the fixture-level contract test.

evidence_id.description: Must match the bound plan's evidence_id (plan.schema.json). This is the explicit counterpart the #1715 review found missing: a plan names an evidence_id, and the evidence bundle now names the same id back.

artifact_ref.description: Bounded, offline-only reference to actual raw bytes. Frozen to fixture_file only in v1 (#1715 revision-2 review point 6: inline_base64 was speculative, unused, and its exclusivity with fixture_file was prose-only). NEVER a URL, host path outside the fixtures tree, or any form of network/live-store resolution.

fingerprint_count.description: sha256 here is a DER fingerprint (sha256 of the base64-decoded certificate body), never a raw-PEM-section hash. tests/trust_operation_v1_contract.rs independently re-derives and cross-checks this; it does not trust the declared value.

source.description: v1 ships no live collector; ordinary non-fixture runs never produce a caro_observed observation for file content. caro_observed is reserved for Caro's own existing process-result observation (exit status of a step), never for a verified filesystem read — enforced below: caro_observed forbids content_hash, artifact_ref, and certificate_fingerprints. CRITICAL (per #1715 revision-2 review point 4): no code path in v1 can actually PRODUCE a caro_observed observation — there is no live collector yet. Every observation in this repo's fixtures with source=caro_observed is a HYPOTHETICAL stand-in for what a future real collector would write, used only to exercise this schema's shape. A caller supplying caro_observed in a hand-written evidence file is, until that collector ships, exactly as unauthoritative as supplied — labeling it caro_observed does not and must not make it self-authenticating.

step_status.description: Required on every observation (previously optional; the #1715 review flagged this). A content-only observation (e.g. step=before) uses completed to mean 'this read was captured', not that a mutation occurred.

step_snapshot_id.description: Identifier scoped to (step, step_snapshot_id): two observations with the same step and a different step_snapshot_id are competing/stale claims about that step, not two facets of the same snapshot. Used to detect a substituted or stale before/backup/staging/final snapshot. Renamed from the prior ambiguous 'snapshot_identity' field (#1715 review).

capture_sequence.description: Monotonic sequence number within this evidence bundle. Used for ordering only; not itself proof of freshness.

capture_time.description: RFC3339 timestamp if supplied. A timestamp alone never proves freshness.

normalized_destination_binding.description: Must be byte-for-byte equal to the bound plan's normalized_destination for this observation to be considered bound to that plan; otherwise it is unbound (stale_observation).

context_binding.description: Must be structurally (deep-)equal to the bound plan's context_identity for this observation to be considered bound to that plan.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the observed raw bytes at this step, when content was captured. Must be null when source=caro_observed (see allOf below).

artifact_ref.description: The actual raw bytes this observation's content_hash was computed from, bounded and offline-only (see definitions.artifact_ref). Required whenever content_hash is non-null, so every content claim resolves to real bytes the contract test can re-hash and compare, not just an asserted digest.

metadata.description: Null, or a COMPLETE metadata triple. Fixes the #1715 round-4 review's point 4 finding that this object had no `required`, so `{}` (metadata present but empty) satisfied the 'metadata must not be null' allOf rule below without actually carrying owner/group/mode.

backup_readability.description: Required and non-null when step=backup (see allOf below). Per #1715 revision-2 review point 3: a completed backup claim needs OBSERVED readability, not merely the presence of metadata. unobserved means exactly that -- an unobserved backup cannot be claimed step_status=completed (see allOf).

consumes_before_snapshot_id.description: Required (may be null only when not applicable) when step=install: the step_snapshot_id of the 'before' observation this install step read its pre-mutation state from. tests/trust_operation_v1_contract.rs checks this names an ACTUAL before observation present earlier (by capture_sequence) in the same bundle -- a dangling or forward reference is stale_observation.

consumes_staging_snapshot_id.description: Required (may be null only when not applicable) when step=install: the step_snapshot_id of the 'stage' observation this install step actually installed. Same freshness/order check as consumes_before_snapshot_id.

authorization_claim.description: A supplied claim of approval. Data only; never itself an executor authorization token. See report.authorization provenance rules (R6/R7 in report.schema.json): this can only ever surface as provenance=supplied_claim, never confirmed_scoped.

host_permission_claim.description: A supplied claim about host authorization. Never promoted to report.host_permission.state=granted with provenance other than supplied_claim or fixture.

allOf.$comment: caro_observed is restricted to process/step-status observations, never to a content claim. Fixes the #1715 review finding: 'external source claims caro_observed'.
A non-null content_hash must resolve to real bytes, not a bare asserted digest.
A backup-step observation always declares its readability, observed or not.

A backup-step observation that claims completed must carry its metadata AND an OBSERVED-readable backup, not merely metadata presence. Fixes #1715 revision-2 review point 3 ('Backup evidence needs OBSERVED readability').

An install-step observation must name which before/staging snapshot it actually consumed, so a stale or substituted snapshot can be detected (#1715 revision-2 review point 3: 'explicit pre-install before/staging snapshot bindings').
